name: Question 14
problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $1\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(2,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}$ seconds.
worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $a$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=a(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(a,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $a=2$ and $\omega =1\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ a(t) & =(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\,i-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\,j \\  & =-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}\,i-\frac{2}{2}\,j \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\,i-\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

A particle P moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at O in the xy-plane with a constant angular velocity of 1rad/s. Given that the particle is located at (2,0) when t=0, find the acceleration of the particle at t=π6 seconds.

a
3i−j
b
−32i+12j
c
−3i−j
d
−12i+32j
e
i−3j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius a in the xy-plane with a constant angular velocity ω is given by r(t)=a(cos⁡ωti+sin⁡ωtj), where it is assumed that the circle is centered at O, and the particle is at the position (a,0) when t=0.

In our case, we have a=2 and ω=1 rad/s, so we get that the position function is given by r(t)=2(cos⁡ti+sin⁡tj).

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

v(t)=(2(cos⁡ti+sin⁡tj))′=−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tja(t)=(−2sin⁡ti+2cos⁡tj)′=−2cos⁡ti−2sin⁡tj.

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at t=π6, as follows: a(π6)=−2cos⁡(π6)i−2sin⁡(π6)j=−232i−22j=−3i−j
